  restore_source() {
    if [ -f "$backup_dir/sources.list" ]; then
      $(prefix_cmd) cp -a "$backup_dir/sources.list" /etc/apt/sources.list || true
    fi
    if [ -f "$backup_dir/ubuntu.sources" ]; then
      $(prefix_cmd) cp -a "$backup_dir/ubuntu.sources" /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources || true
    fi
  }
  update_apt_sources() {
    local host=$1
    local apt_file=$2
    # || true: a sed failure on one sources file (read-only fs,
    # immutable bit, full tmpfs) shouldn't kill the whole step;
    # restore_source will undo any partial edits on the next
    # iteration of the candidate-mirror loop.
    $(prefix_cmd) sed -i -E "s|https?://[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\.ubuntu\.com/ubuntu|http://$host/ubuntu|g" "$apt_file" || true
  }
  # Surface /tmp/apt-update.log to the pod's stderr on failure.
  # Without this, users only see the terse summary line — the
  # actual apt error stays inside the (often torn-down) pod.
  dump_apt_log() {
    local log=/tmp/apt-update.log
    if [ -f "$log" ]; then
      echo "=== /tmp/apt-update.log (last 200 lines) ===" >&2
      tail -n 200 "$log" >&2 || true
      echo "=== end /tmp/apt-update.log ===" >&2
    else
      echo "/tmp/apt-update.log not found" >&2
    fi
  }
  # FUSE compatibility: we want libfuse2 (FUSE 2 ABI for legacy
  # clients like older s3fs/sshfs) AND fuse3 (binary + libfuse3-3
  # for hf-mount, rclone, blobfuse2, etc.). On Ubuntu 22.04+
  # `fuse3 Breaks: fuse` (both ship /usr/bin/fusermount), so the
  # two packages cannot coexist. FUSE is handled out-of-band below.
  PACKAGES="rsync curl wget netcat gcc patch pciutils openssh-server";

  # --- Portable package-manager support (CC-328 / TICKET-039) ---
  # This bootstrap historically assumed apt/dpkg (Debian/Ubuntu).
  # Detect the image's package manager, gate installs on BINARY
  # presence (`command -v`) rather than `dpkg -l`, and dispatch the
  # install through the right tool. Effect: a non-Debian image
  # (RHEL/UBI/Alpine/SUSE) that already ships the prereqs needs no
  # install at all; one that's missing them installs via dnf/apk/etc.
  # The apt path is UNCHANGED — INSTALL_FIRST/MISSING carry generic
  # names and map_pkg_names() translates them back to the exact apt
  # names (e.g. netcat -> netcat-openbsd) the old code used, so
  # Debian/Ubuntu behavior is byte-for-byte identical.
  PKG_MGR=""
  if   command -v apt-get  >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=apt
  elif command -v dnf      >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=dnf
  elif command -v microdnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=microdnf
  elif command -v yum      >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=yum
  elif command -v apk      >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=apk
  elif command -v zypper   >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=zypper
  fi

  # Is a generic package present? Prove via its BINARY (portable
  # across distros; `dpkg -l` doesn't exist on RHEL/Alpine/SUSE).
  pkg_present() {
    case "$1" in
      netcat)         command -v nc          >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
      # sshd/lspci live in /usr/sbin|/sbin, which a non-root user's
      # PATH often omits -- fall back to absolute paths so an
      # already-present tool isn't needlessly (re)installed.
      openssh-server) command -v sshd  >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x /usr/sbin/sshd ]  || [ -x /sbin/sshd ]  ;;
      pciutils)       command -v lspci >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x /usr/sbin/lspci ] || [ -x /sbin/lspci ] ;;
      fuse)           command -v fusermount  >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
      fuse3)          command -v fusermount3 >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
      *)              command -v "$1"        >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
    esac
  }

  # Translate generic package names to per-manager names. apt names
  # match the SkyPilot defaults (so the apt path is unchanged); the
  # non-apt managers need a few translations.
  map_pkg_names() {
    local out="" g
    for g in "$@"; do
      case "$g" in
        netcat)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            dnf|yum|microdnf) out="$out nmap-ncat" ;;
            *)                out="$out netcat-openbsd" ;;
          esac ;;
        fuse)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            dnf|yum|microdnf) out="$out fuse fuse-libs" ;;
            *)                out="$out fuse" ;;
          esac ;;
        fuse3)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            dnf|yum|microdnf) out="$out fuse3 fuse3-libs" ;;
            *)                out="$out fuse3" ;;
          esac ;;
        openssh-server)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            apk|zypper) out="$out openssh" ;;
            *)          out="$out openssh-server" ;;
          esac ;;
        *) out="$out $g" ;;
      esac
    done
    echo "$out"
  }

  # Install with the detected NON-apt manager under a sanitized loader
  # environment: a conda/custom image can put its own libs ahead on
  # LD_LIBRARY_PATH/PATH and break the system dnf/yum itself (e.g.
  # `libdnf.so.2: undefined symbol: repo_add_rpm`; or a baked
  # LD_PRELOAD like libnccl.so breaking the manager's Python with a
  # GLIBCXX error). Drop the loader-pollution vars and pin a system
  # PATH, but KEEP http(s)_proxy/no_proxy + CA env so proxied clusters
  # can still reach their repos. (apt keeps its own mirror-fallback.)
  pkg_install() {
    local names; names="$(map_pkg_names "$@")"
    local CLEAN="env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH -u LD_PRELOAD -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"
    case "$PKG_MGR" in
      dnf|yum)  $(prefix_cmd) $CLEAN "$PKG_MGR" install -y $names ;;
      microdnf) $(prefix_cmd) $CLEAN microdnf install -y $names ;;
      apk)      $(prefix_cmd) $CLEAN apk add --no-cache $names ;;
      zypper)   $(prefix_cmd) $CLEAN zypper --non-interactive install $names ;;
      *)        return 1 ;;
    esac
  }

  # Separate packages into two groups: packages that are installed first
  # so that curl, rsync, ssh and wget are available sooner to unblock the following
  # conda installation and rsync.
  set -e
  INSTALL_FIRST="";
  MISSING_PACKAGES="";
  for pkg in $PACKAGES; do
    pkg_present "$pkg" && continue
    # curl/rsync/wget are core (needed early to unblock conda + rsync).
    # Everything else — incl. netcat — is best-effort: worker readiness
    # uses bash /dev/tcp (not `nc`), so netcat is not a launch blocker,
    # and its per-distro name (nmap-ncat / netcat-openbsd) can't fail
    # the launch.
    case "$pkg" in
      curl|rsync|wget) INSTALL_FIRST="$INSTALL_FIRST $pkg" ;;
      *)               MISSING_PACKAGES="$MISSING_PACKAGES $pkg" ;;
    esac
  done;

  # No core package missing => the image already ships curl (and
  # whatever trust store its curl uses), so STEP 2 has nothing to
  # wait for. Publish the marker HERE, not only on the install
  # paths, because several of those can bail out without being
  # fatal and would otherwise leave STEP 2 waiting forever:
  #   - apt with INSTALL_FIRST empty but MISSING_PACKAGES set: the
  #     index refresh can fail on every mirror and `continue` out
  #     of the loop, yet the core-install guard below only exits
  #     when INSTALL_FIRST is non-empty, so STEP 1 still ends 0.
  #   - no supported package manager at all: same shape.
  # Both cases are ones the old `command -v curl` gate passed
  # immediately, so not publishing here would be a regression.
  # Deliberately before the FUSE block below: `fuse` can be
  # appended to INSTALL_FIRST, but it has nothing to do with the
  # HTTPS conda download STEP 2 is gating on.
  if [ -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
    touch "$CORE_PKGS_READY"
  fi

  # FUSE handling — four cases for (fuse_installed, fuse3_installed):
  #   (0, 0): install fuse first then fuse3. apt's Breaks
  #           resolution removes the `fuse` package while leaving
  #           libfuse2 → final state: libfuse2 (FUSE 2 ABI) +
  #           fuse3 (binary + libfuse3-3 for FUSE 3 ABI).
  #   (1, 0): only fuse3 missing. Queue it in MISSING_PACKAGES;
  #           apt removes `fuse` package but libfuse2 survives.
  #   (0, 1): already the desired state (SkyPilot default images).
  #           User-supplied images may lack libfuse2, need to handle
  #           this.
  #   (1, 1): impossible on Ubuntu 22.04+ (Breaks declaration);
  #           treated as no-op for forward-compat.
  

  # Detect distro for mirror fallback
  APT_OS="unknown"
  if [ -f /etc/os-release ]; then
    . /etc/os-release
    case "$ID" in
      debian) APT_OS="debian" ;;
      ubuntu) APT_OS="ubuntu" ;;
      *)
        if [ -n "$ID_LIKE" ]; then
          case " $ID $ID_LIKE " in
            *ubuntu*) APT_OS="ubuntu" ;;
            *debian*) APT_OS="debian" ;;
          esac
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  fi

  # Build candidate list: default (empty string) first, then mirrors for ubuntu.
  # deb.debian.org is a CDN endpoint, if one backend goes down,
  # the CDN automatically fails over to another mirror,
  # so we only add mirror candidates for ubuntu here.
  # Selected from https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+archivemirrors
  # and results from apt-select
  
  MIRROR_CANDIDATES=""
  if [ "$APT_OS" = "ubuntu" ]; then
    MIRROR_CANDIDATES="mirrors.wikimedia.org mirror.umd.edu"
  fi
  

  # Wrap the candidate-mirror loop in a function so we can
  # short-circuit when nothing needs installing.
  run_apt_install_with_fallback() {
  INSTALL_SUCCESS=false
  backup_source
  for candidate in "" $MIRROR_CANDIDATES; do
    restore_source
    if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
      echo "Trying APT mirror ($APT_OS): $candidate" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
      found_sources=false
      if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list ]; then
        update_apt_sources $candidate /etc/apt/sources.list
        found_sources=true
      fi
      if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources ]; then
        update_apt_sources $candidate /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources
        found_sources=true
      fi
      if [ "$found_sources" = "false" ]; then
        echo "Error: no apt sources file found" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
        dump_apt_log
        break
      fi
    fi

    # Try INSTALL_FIRST (required core packages)
    if [ ! -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
      echo "Installing core packages: $(map_pkg_names $INSTALL_FIRST)" >> /tmp/apt-update.log;
      apt_update_install_with_retries $(map_pkg_names $INSTALL_FIRST) >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || {
        echo "Install failed with ${candidate:-default sources}: $INSTALL_FIRST" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
        continue
      }
    else
      # No core packages to install, but we still need to update the
      # package index for MISSING_PACKAGES.
      apt_update_with_retries >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || {
        echo "apt-get update failed with ${candidate:-default sources}" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
        continue
      }
    fi

    # INSTALL_FIRST succeeded (or was empty) with this source.
    # Core prereqs are configured -- unblock STEP 2 now, before the
    # best-effort packages below.
    touch "$CORE_PKGS_READY"
    # Install MISSING_PACKAGES individually (optional, some may not exist on certain distros).
    set +e
    if [ ! -z "$MISSING_PACKAGES" ]; then
      echo "Installing missing packages individually: $MISSING_PACKAGES" >> /tmp/apt-update.log;
      for pkg in $MISSING_PACKAGES; do
        apt_install_with_retries $(map_pkg_names $pkg) >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || echo "Optional package $pkg installation failed, skip." >> /tmp/apt-update.log;
      done
    fi

    INSTALL_SUCCESS=true
    break
  done
  restore_source
  }

  # Non-apt install path (dnf/microdnf/yum/apk/zypper): mirror the
  # apt path's INSTALL_FIRST (fatal) / MISSING (best-effort) split.
  run_pkg_install_nonapt() {
    INSTALL_SUCCESS=false
    if [ ! -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
      echo "Installing core packages via $PKG_MGR: $INSTALL_FIRST" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
      # Retry, to match the apt path (which retries across mirror
      # candidates). A single transient repo/CDN/proxy failure
      # should not kill the launch.
      _core_try=0
      while :; do
        # `|| true` is load-bearing, not defensive: this function
        # runs under the `set -e` from the top of the install
        # section (unlike the apt path, which drops to `set +e`
        # inside its own helper). As a standalone command,
        # a non-zero pkg_install would abort STEP 1 right here --
        # before the _core_missing check, the sleep, or any retry
        # -- so the pod would fail with .failed instead of
        # retrying, defeating the point of this loop. It also
        # matters for zypper, whose >=100 informational-success
        # codes are non-zero. The exit status is deliberately
        # ignored; pkg_present below is what decides success.
        pkg_install $INSTALL_FIRST >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || true
        # Do NOT trust the exit status alone: zypper returns >=100
        # for informational success (e.g. 106 = a repo had to be
        # skipped, but the requested packages installed fine), and
        # a partially unreachable repo set is normal behind an
        # egress proxy. Ask the same portable question the install
        # decision asked -- is the package actually there now?
        _core_missing=""
        for _g in $INSTALL_FIRST; do
          pkg_present "$_g" || _core_missing="$_core_missing $_g"
        done
        if [ -z "$_core_missing" ]; then
          break
        fi
        _core_try=$((_core_try + 1))
        if [ "$_core_try" -ge 3 ]; then
          echo "Core install failed via $PKG_MGR after $_core_try attempts; still missing:$_core_missing" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
          return
        fi
        echo "Core packages still missing:$_core_missing -- retry $_core_try/3 via $PKG_MGR" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
        sleep 5
      done
    fi
    # Core prereqs are configured -- unblock STEP 2 before the
    # best-effort packages below.
    touch "$CORE_PKGS_READY"
    if [ ! -z "$MISSING_PACKAGES" ]; then
      echo "Installing missing packages individually via $PKG_MGR: $MISSING_PACKAGES" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
      for pkg in $MISSING_PACKAGES; do
        pkg_install $pkg >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || echo "Optional package $pkg installation failed via $PKG_MGR, skip." >> /tmp/apt-update.log
      done
    fi
    INSTALL_SUCCESS=true
  }

  INSTALL_SUCCESS=false
  if [ -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ] && [ -z "$MISSING_PACKAGES" ]; then
    echo "All required packages already installed; skipping package install." >> /tmp/apt-update.log
    # ($CORE_PKGS_READY was already published above, since
    # INSTALL_FIRST is empty on this path.)
    INSTALL_SUCCESS=true
  elif [ "$PKG_MGR" = "apt" ]; then
    run_apt_install_with_fallback
  elif [ -n "$PKG_MGR" ]; then
    run_pkg_install_nonapt
  else
    echo "Error: no supported package manager (apt/dnf/microdnf/yum/apk/zypper) found and prereqs are missing: $INSTALL_FIRST $MISSING_PACKAGES" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
  fi
  # Re-arm set -e for the SSH setup below. The apt fallback helper
  # leaves set +e behind, and the non-apt / already-installed paths
  # must not differ from each other -- but the state they converge
  # on has to be set -e, because upstream ran this block under
  # set -e and the commands in it are load-bearing: if the
  # sshd_config edit, ssh-keygen or authorized_keys write fails,
  # SkyPilot cannot reach the pod at all. Swallowing those turns a
  # clear "apt-ssh-setup failed" into an opaque SSH timeout much
  # later. The genuinely optional Debian-isms are tolerated
  # individually with `|| true` at their own call sites instead.
  set -e

  if [ "$INSTALL_SUCCESS" = "false" ] && [ ! -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
    echo "Error: core package installation failed across all sources." >> /tmp/apt-update.log
    dump_apt_log
    exit 1
  fi;

  

  

  $(prefix_cmd) mkdir -p /var/run/sshd;
  $(prefix_cmd) sed -i "s/PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/" /etc/ssh/sshd_config;
  # Cosmetic (silences a pam_loginuid warning in containers); not
  # required for SSH to work, and /etc/pam.d/sshd need not exist on
  # a minimal non-Debian image -- so tolerate it rather than
  # dropping set -e for the load-bearing commands below.
  $(prefix_cmd) sed "s@session\s*required\s*pam_loginuid.so@session optional pam_loginuid.so@g" -i /etc/pam.d/sshd || true;
  cd /etc/ssh/ && $(prefix_cmd) ssh-keygen -A;
  $(prefix_cmd) mkdir -p ~/.ssh;
  $(prefix_cmd) chown -R $(whoami) ~/.ssh;
  $(prefix_cmd) chmod 700 ~/.ssh;
  $(prefix_cmd) cat > ~/.ssh/authorized_keys <<'SKYPILOT_SSH_KEY_EOF'
ssh-rsa 
SKYPILOT_SSH_KEY_EOF
  $(prefix_cmd) chmod 644 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys;
  # Start sshd portably: the service is `ssh` on Debian/Ubuntu but
  # `sshd` on RHEL/UBI/SUSE, and minimal containers often have no
  # service manager at all — fall back to launching the daemon
  # directly. `|| true` so a benign restart failure never aborts.
  $(prefix_cmd) service ssh restart 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) service sshd restart 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) systemctl restart ssh 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) systemctl restart sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) kill -HUP $(cat /var/run/sshd.pid 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) /usr/sbin/sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) /sbin/sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || true;
  # Also cosmetic, and ~/.profile is a Debian convention (RHEL ships
  # ~/.bash_profile) -- tolerate a missing file.
  $(prefix_cmd) sed -i "s/mesg n/tty -s \&\& mesg n/" ~/.profile || true;

  

  touch /tmp/apt_ssh_setup_complete
  echo "=== SSH setup completed ==="
  ) > /tmp/${STEPS[0]}.log 2>&1
  if [ "$?" -ne "0" ]; then
    {
    echo "Error: ${STEPS[0]} failed. Continuing anyway..." > /tmp/${STEPS[0]}.failed 2>&1
    cat /tmp/${STEPS[0]}.log
    exit 1
    }
  fi
) &

# STEP 2: Install conda, ray and skypilot (for dependencies); start
# ray cluster.
(
  (
  set -e
  # Create $SKY_RUNTIME_DIR/.sky early — uv_installation_commands
  # writes python_path there before ray_installation_commands (which
  # contains SETUP_SKY_DIRS_COMMANDS) creates it.
  mkdir -p ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky
  # Wait for STEP 1 to have INSTALLED AND CONFIGURED the core
  # prereqs before the HTTPS conda download below.
  #
  # This gate used to be `dpkg -l | grep "^ii  curl "`, which
  # protected the download somewhat by accident: waiting for curl
  # to be *configured* implied ca-certificates (pulled in the same
  # apt transaction) had already run update-ca-certificates, so
  # /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt existed. A portable
  # `command -v curl` loses exactly that -- the binary is unpacked
  # BEFORE the configure phase -- so the download could fire with
  # no trust store and die with
  #   curl: (77) error setting certificate verify locations
  # which short-circuits conda installation and leaves the
  # unconditional `conda deactivate` in
  # CONDA_INSTALLATION_COMMANDS as a command-not-found. Repro'd on
  # a bare apt image (--image-id docker:ubuntu:18.04).
  #
  # Reintroducing the dpkg check is not an option: it is apt-only
  # (the point of this patch is RHEL/UBI/Alpine/SUSE), and it would
  # now DEADLOCK -- the install decision in STEP 1 uses binary
  # presence, so an image shipping curl outside dpkg is never
  # queued for install and a dpkg-state wait would spin forever.
  #
  # So gate on STEP 1's own marker instead. That is the package
  # manager reporting it returned, which is the "fully configured"
  # guarantee itself rather than a proxy for it -- portable across
  # apt/dnf/microdnf/yum/apk/zypper, and it needs no timeout or
  # per-distro CA paths. Also break out if STEP 1 failed, so this
  # can never outlive the step it waits on.
  until [ -f "$CORE_PKGS_READY" ] || [ -f "/tmp/${STEPS[0]}.failed" ]; do
    sleep 0.1
  done
  
  UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv -V >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | UV_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" sh;[ -d ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime ] || UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv venv --seed ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime --python 3.10;echo "$(echo ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime)/bin/python" > ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path;
  UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv -V >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | UV_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" sh;mkdir -p ~/sky_workdir && mkdir -p ~/.sky/sky_app && mkdir -p ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky;echo PATH=$PATH; VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv pip install "setuptools<70"; VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv pip install "click<8.3.0"; VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv pip list | grep "ray " | grep 2.9.3 2>&1 > /dev/null || RAY_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:6380 env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME $([ -s ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path ] && cat ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path 2> /dev/null || command -v python3) $([ -s ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/ray_path ] && cat ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/ray_path 2> /dev/null || command -v ray) status || VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv pip install -U "ray[default]==2.9.3" "pydantic-core==2.41.1" "click<8.3.0"; export PATH=$PATH:${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.local/bin; [ -s ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/ray_path ] || { VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv run --no-project --no-config sh -c "command -v ray" > ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/ray_path || exit 1; }; 

  # set UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON to false in case the user provided docker image set it to true.
  # unset PYTHONPATH and set CWD to $HOME to avoid user image interfering with SkyPilot runtime.
  VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME ~/.local/bin/uv pip install skypilot[kubernetes,remote]
  # Wait (bounded) for the best-effort `patch` install to land
  # before applying the Ray patches. An image may ship no `patch`
  # and have no usable repo, so proceed after 60s rather than hang
  # this step forever; the apply below is best-effort (see there).
  _patch_wait=0
  until command -v patch >/dev/null 2>&1; do
    sleep 0.1
    _patch_wait=$((_patch_wait + 1))
    if [ "$_patch_wait" -ge 600 ]; then
      echo "WARNING: patch not installed after 60s; proceeding."
      break
    fi
    # Throttle the notice to ~once every 5s (loop runs at 10Hz) so a
    # slow install doesn't flood the pod log 10x/second.
    if [ $((_patch_wait % 50)) -eq 1 ]; then
      echo "Waiting for patch package to be installed..."
    fi
  done
  # Apply Ray patches (quality-of-life fixes: progress bar, log
  # streaming). The patch payload is carried in this pod spec, not
  # read out of the installed `sky`: this runs before the SkyPilot
  # wheel is uploaded, so the only `sky` on the node is whatever
  # `pip install skypilot` resolved to -- an unrelated release,

function mylsof { p=$(for pid in /proc/{0..9}*; do i=$(basename "$pid"); for file in "$pid"/fd/*; do link=$(readlink -e "$file"); if [ "$link" = "$1" ]; then echo "$i"; fi; done; done); echo "$p"; };

# Tails file and checks every 5 sec for
# open file handlers with write access
# closes if none exist
monitor_file() {
  local file="$1"
  tail -f "$file" &
  TAIL_PID=$!
  while kill -0 $TAIL_PID 2> /dev/null; do
    # only two PIDs should be accessing the file
    # the log appender and log tailer
    if [ $(mylsof "$file" | wc -l) -lt 2 ]; then
      kill $TAIL_PID
      break
    fi
    # Sleep for 5 seconds before checking again. Do not make this
    # too short as it will consume CPU, and too long will cause
    # the file to be closed too late keeping the pod alive.
    sleep 5
  done
}

log_tail() {
  # Use a bash glob (not `ls $(eval echo ...)`) so we are
  # safe against ARG_MAX at very high file counts and against
  # spaces in $HOME or in any path component. nullglob makes
  # an empty match a no-op instead of yielding the literal
  # pattern. log_tail is launched via `log_tail &`, so this
  # runs in its own subshell and the shopt does not leak.
  shopt -s nullglob

  # O(1) membership set. Replaces an `echo $str | grep -q` check
  # that was O(n) per file (O(n^2) across the outer loop).
  local -A already_monitored

  # Pre-seed with every file that exists at startup so we do NOT
  # spawn monitor_file for them. On an HA controller pod restart
  # the PVC retains task logs from all prior (completed) jobs;
  # tailing them all spawns a tail+mylsof loop per file, and
  # mylsof's /proc/*/fd/* scan grows with the process count,
  # producing runaway fork growth.
  for f in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log; do
    already_monitored["$f"]=1
  done

  # Wait until at least one log file exists.
  while true; do
    for f in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log; do
      break 2
    done
    sleep 1
  done

  # Infinite loop to continuously check for new files
  while true; do
    for file in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log; do
      if [[ -n "${already_monitored[$file]:-}" ]]; then
        # File is already being monitored
        continue
      fi

      # Monitor the new file
      monitor_file "$file" &
      already_monitored["$file"]=1
    done
    sleep 0.1
  done
}

# polling their completion/failure markers. If any step fails,
# exit the container so the pod enters a failed state instead
# of hanging indefinitely.

    local delay=1
    local i
    for i in $(seq 1 $tries); do

        netcat)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            dnf|yum|microdnf) out="$out nmap-ncat" ;;
            *)                out="$out netcat-openbsd" ;;
          esac ;;
        fuse)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            dnf|yum|microdnf) out="$out fuse fuse-libs" ;;
            *)                out="$out fuse" ;;
          esac ;;
        fuse3)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            dnf|yum|microdnf) out="$out fuse3 fuse3-libs" ;;
            *)                out="$out fuse3" ;;
          esac ;;
        openssh-server)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            apk|zypper) out="$out openssh" ;;
            *)          out="$out openssh-server" ;;
          esac ;;
        *) out="$out $g" ;;
      esac
    done
    echo "$out"
  }

  # Install with the detected NON-apt manager under a sanitized loader
  # environment: a conda/custom image can put its own libs ahead on
  # LD_LIBRARY_PATH/PATH and break the system dnf/yum itself (e.g.
  # `libdnf.so.2: undefined symbol: repo_add_rpm`; or a baked
  # LD_PRELOAD like libnccl.so breaking the manager's Python with a
  # GLIBCXX error). Drop the loader-pollution vars and pin a system
  # PATH, but KEEP http(s)_proxy/no_proxy + CA env so proxied clusters
  # can still reach their repos. (apt keeps its own mirror-fallback.)
  pkg_install() {
    local names; names="$(map_pkg_names "$@")"
    local CLEAN="env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH -u LD_PRELOAD -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"
    case "$PKG_MGR" in
      dnf|yum)  $(prefix_cmd) $CLEAN "$PKG_MGR" install -y $names ;;
      microdnf) $(prefix_cmd) $CLEAN microdnf install -y $names ;;
      apk)      $(prefix_cmd) $CLEAN apk add --no-cache $names ;;
      zypper)   $(prefix_cmd) $CLEAN zypper --non-interactive install $names ;;
      *)        return 1 ;;
    esac
  }

  # Separate packages into two groups: packages that are installed first
  # so that curl, rsync, ssh and wget are available sooner to unblock the following
  # conda installation and rsync.
  set -e
  INSTALL_FIRST="";
  MISSING_PACKAGES="";
  for pkg in $PACKAGES; do
    pkg_present "$pkg" && continue
    # curl/rsync/wget are core (needed early to unblock conda + rsync).
    # Everything else — incl. netcat — is best-effort: worker readiness
    # uses bash /dev/tcp (not `nc`), so netcat is not a launch blocker,
    # and its per-distro name (nmap-ncat / netcat-openbsd) can't fail
    # the launch.
    case "$pkg" in
      curl|rsync|wget) INSTALL_FIRST="$INSTALL_FIRST $pkg" ;;
      *)               MISSING_PACKAGES="$MISSING_PACKAGES $pkg" ;;
    esac
  done;

  # No core package missing => the image already ships curl (and
  # whatever trust store its curl uses), so STEP 2 has nothing to
  # wait for. Publish the marker HERE, not only on the install
  # paths, because several of those can bail out without being
  # fatal and would otherwise leave STEP 2 waiting forever:
  #   - apt with INSTALL_FIRST empty but MISSING_PACKAGES set: the
  #     index refresh can fail on every mirror and `continue` out
  #     of the loop, yet the core-install guard below only exits
  #     when INSTALL_FIRST is non-empty, so STEP 1 still ends 0.
  #   - no supported package manager at all: same shape.
  # Both cases are ones the old `command -v curl` gate passed
  # immediately, so not publishing here would be a regression.
  # Deliberately before the FUSE block below: `fuse` can be
  # appended to INSTALL_FIRST, but it has nothing to do with the
  # HTTPS conda download STEP 2 is gating on.
  if [ -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
    touch "$CORE_PKGS_READY"
  fi

  # FUSE handling — four cases for (fuse_installed, fuse3_installed):
  #   (0, 0): install fuse first then fuse3. apt's Breaks
  #           resolution removes the `fuse` package while leaving
  #           libfuse2 → final state: libfuse2 (FUSE 2 ABI) +
  #           fuse3 (binary + libfuse3-3 for FUSE 3 ABI).
  #   (1, 0): only fuse3 missing. Queue it in MISSING_PACKAGES;
  #           apt removes `fuse` package but libfuse2 survives.
  #   (0, 1): already the desired state (SkyPilot default images).
  #           User-supplied images may lack libfuse2, need to handle
  #           this.
  #   (1, 1): impossible on Ubuntu 22.04+ (Breaks declaration);
  #           treated as no-op for forward-compat.
  

  # Detect distro for mirror fallback
  APT_OS="unknown"
  if [ -f /etc/os-release ]; then
    . /etc/os-release
    case "$ID" in
      debian) APT_OS="debian" ;;
      ubuntu) APT_OS="ubuntu" ;;
      *)
        if [ -n "$ID_LIKE" ]; then
          case " $ID $ID_LIKE " in
            *ubuntu*) APT_OS="ubuntu" ;;
            *debian*) APT_OS="debian" ;;
          esac
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  fi

  # Build candidate list: default (empty string) first, then mirrors for ubuntu.
  # deb.debian.org is a CDN endpoint, if one backend goes down,
  # the CDN automatically fails over to another mirror,
  # so we only add mirror candidates for ubuntu here.
  # Selected from https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+archivemirrors
  # and results from apt-select
  
  MIRROR_CANDIDATES=""
  if [ "$APT_OS" = "ubuntu" ]; then
    MIRROR_CANDIDATES="mirrors.wikimedia.org mirror.umd.edu"
  fi
  

  # Wrap the candidate-mirror loop in a function so we can
  # short-circuit when nothing needs installing.
  run_apt_install_with_fallback() {
  INSTALL_SUCCESS=false
  backup_source
  for candidate in "" $MIRROR_CANDIDATES; do
    restore_source
    if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
      echo "Trying APT mirror ($APT_OS): $candidate" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
      found_sources=false
      if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list ]; then
        update_apt_sources $candidate /etc/apt/sources.list
        found_sources=true
      fi
      if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources ]; then
        update_apt_sources $candidate /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources
        found_sources=true
      fi
      if [ "$found_sources" = "false" ]; then
        echo "Error: no apt sources file found" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
        dump_apt_log
        break
      fi
    fi

    # Try INSTALL_FIRST (required core packages)
    if [ ! -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
      echo "Installing core packages: $(map_pkg_names $INSTALL_FIRST)" >> /tmp/apt-update.log;
      apt_update_install_with_retries $(map_pkg_names $INSTALL_FIRST) >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || {
        echo "Install failed with ${candidate:-default sources}: $INSTALL_FIRST" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
        continue
      }
    else
      # No core packages to install, but we still need to update the
      # package index for MISSING_PACKAGES.
      apt_update_with_retries >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || {
        echo "apt-get update failed with ${candidate:-default sources}" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
        continue
      }
    fi

    # INSTALL_FIRST succeeded (or was empty) with this source.
    # Core prereqs are configured -- unblock STEP 2 now, before the
    # best-effort packages below.
    touch "$CORE_PKGS_READY"
    # Install MISSING_PACKAGES individually (optional, some may not exist on certain distros).
    set +e
    if [ ! -z "$MISSING_PACKAGES" ]; then
      echo "Installing missing packages individually: $MISSING_PACKAGES" >> /tmp/apt-update.log;
      for pkg in $MISSING_PACKAGES; do
        apt_install_with_retries $(map_pkg_names $pkg) >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || echo "Optional package $pkg installation failed, skip." >> /tmp/apt-update.log;
      done
    fi

    INSTALL_SUCCESS=true
    break
  done
  restore_source
  }

  # Non-apt install path (dnf/microdnf/yum/apk/zypper): mirror the
  # apt path's INSTALL_FIRST (fatal) / MISSING (best-effort) split.
  run_pkg_install_nonapt() {
    INSTALL_SUCCESS=false
    if [ ! -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
      echo "Installing core packages via $PKG_MGR: $INSTALL_FIRST" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
      # Retry, to match the apt path (which retries across mirror
      # candidates). A single transient repo/CDN/proxy failure
      # should not kill the launch.
      _core_try=0
      while :; do
        # `|| true` is load-bearing, not defensive: this function
        # runs under the `set -e` from the top of the install
        # section (unlike the apt path, which drops to `set +e`
        # inside its own helper). As a standalone command,
        # a non-zero pkg_install would abort STEP 1 right here --
        # before the _core_missing check, the sleep, or any retry
        # -- so the pod would fail with .failed instead of
        # retrying, defeating the point of this loop. It also
        # matters for zypper, whose >=100 informational-success
        # codes are non-zero. The exit status is deliberately
        # ignored; pkg_present below is what decides success.
        pkg_install $INSTALL_FIRST >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || true
        # Do NOT trust the exit status alone: zypper returns >=100
        # for informational success (e.g. 106 = a repo had to be
        # skipped, but the requested packages installed fine), and
        # a partially unreachable repo set is normal behind an
        # egress proxy. Ask the same portable question the install
        # decision asked -- is the package actually there now?
        _core_missing=""
        for _g in $INSTALL_FIRST; do
          pkg_present "$_g" || _core_missing="$_core_missing $_g"
        done
        if [ -z "$_core_missing" ]; then
          break
        fi
        _core_try=$((_core_try + 1))
        if [ "$_core_try" -ge 3 ]; then
          echo "Core install failed via $PKG_MGR after $_core_try attempts; still missing:$_core_missing" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
          return
        fi
        echo "Core packages still missing:$_core_missing -- retry $_core_try/3 via $PKG_MGR" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
        sleep 5
      done
    fi
    # Core prereqs are configured -- unblock STEP 2 before the
    # best-effort packages below.
    touch "$CORE_PKGS_READY"
    if [ ! -z "$MISSING_PACKAGES" ]; then
      echo "Installing missing packages individually via $PKG_MGR: $MISSING_PACKAGES" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
      for pkg in $MISSING_PACKAGES; do
        pkg_install $pkg >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || echo "Optional package $pkg installation failed via $PKG_MGR, skip." >> /tmp/apt-update.log
      done
    fi
    INSTALL_SUCCESS=true
  }

  INSTALL_SUCCESS=false
  if [ -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ] && [ -z "$MISSING_PACKAGES" ]; then
    echo "All required packages already installed; skipping package install." >> /tmp/apt-update.log
    # ($CORE_PKGS_READY was already published above, since
    # INSTALL_FIRST is empty on this path.)
    INSTALL_SUCCESS=true
  elif [ "$PKG_MGR" = "apt" ]; then
    run_apt_install_with_fallback
  elif [ -n "$PKG_MGR" ]; then
    run_pkg_install_nonapt
  else
    echo "Error: no supported package manager (apt/dnf/microdnf/yum/apk/zypper) found and prereqs are missing: $INSTALL_FIRST $MISSING_PACKAGES" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
  fi
  # Re-arm set -e for the SSH setup below. The apt fallback helper
  # leaves set +e behind, and the non-apt / already-installed paths
  # must not differ from each other -- but the state they converge
  # on has to be set -e, because upstream ran this block under
  # set -e and the commands in it are load-bearing: if the
  # sshd_config edit, ssh-keygen or authorized_keys write fails,
  # SkyPilot cannot reach the pod at all. Swallowing those turns a
  # clear "apt-ssh-setup failed" into an opaque SSH timeout much
  # later. The genuinely optional Debian-isms are tolerated
  # individually with `|| true` at their own call sites instead.
  set -e

  if [ "$INSTALL_SUCCESS" = "false" ] && [ ! -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
    echo "Error: core package installation failed across all sources." >> /tmp/apt-update.log
    dump_apt_log
    exit 1
  fi;

  

  

  $(prefix_cmd) mkdir -p /var/run/sshd;
  $(prefix_cmd) sed -i "s/PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/" /etc/ssh/sshd_config;
  # Cosmetic (silences a pam_loginuid warning in containers); not
  # required for SSH to work, and /etc/pam.d/sshd need not exist on
  # a minimal non-Debian image -- so tolerate it rather than
  # dropping set -e for the load-bearing commands below.
  $(prefix_cmd) sed "s@session\s*required\s*pam_loginuid.so@session optional pam_loginuid.so@g" -i /etc/pam.d/sshd || true;
  cd /etc/ssh/ && $(prefix_cmd) ssh-keygen -A;
  $(prefix_cmd) mkdir -p ~/.ssh;
  $(prefix_cmd) chown -R $(whoami) ~/.ssh;
  $(prefix_cmd) chmod 700 ~/.ssh;
  $(prefix_cmd) cat > ~/.ssh/authorized_keys <<'SKYPILOT_SSH_KEY_EOF'
ssh-rsa 
SKYPILOT_SSH_KEY_EOF
  $(prefix_cmd) chmod 644 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys;
  # Start sshd portably: the service is `ssh` on Debian/Ubuntu but
  # `sshd` on RHEL/UBI/SUSE, and minimal containers often have no
  # service manager at all — fall back to launching the daemon
  # directly. `|| true` so a benign restart failure never aborts.
  $(prefix_cmd) service ssh restart 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) service sshd restart 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) systemctl restart ssh 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) systemctl restart sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) kill -HUP $(cat /var/run/sshd.pid 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) /usr/sbin/sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) /sbin/sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || true;
  # Also cosmetic, and ~/.profile is a Debian convention (RHEL ships
  # ~/.bash_profile) -- tolerate a missing file.
  $(prefix_cmd) sed -i "s/mesg n/tty -s \&\& mesg n/" ~/.profile || true;

  

  touch /tmp/apt_ssh_setup_complete
  echo "=== SSH setup completed ==="
  ) > /tmp/${STEPS[0]}.log 2>&1
  if [ "$?" -ne "0" ]; then
    {
    echo "Error: ${STEPS[0]} failed. Continuing anyway..." > /tmp/${STEPS[0]}.failed 2>&1
    cat /tmp/${STEPS[0]}.log
    exit 1
    }
  fi
) &

# STEP 2: Install conda, ray and skypilot (for dependencies); start
# ray cluster.
(
  (
  set -e
  # Create $SKY_RUNTIME_DIR/.sky early — uv_installation_commands
  # writes python_path there before ray_installation_commands (which
  # contains SETUP_SKY_DIRS_COMMANDS) creates it.
  mkdir -p ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky
  # Wait for STEP 1 to have INSTALLED AND CONFIGURED the core
  # prereqs before the HTTPS conda download below.
  #
  # This gate used to be `dpkg -l | grep "^ii  curl "`, which
  # protected the download somewhat by accident: waiting for curl
  # to be *configured* implied ca-certificates (pulled in the same
  # apt transaction) had already run update-ca-certificates, so
  # /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt existed. A portable
  # `command -v curl` loses exactly that -- the binary is unpacked
  # BEFORE the configure phase -- so the download could fire with
  # no trust store and die with
  #   curl: (77) error setting certificate verify locations
  # which short-circuits conda installation and leaves the
  # unconditional `conda deactivate` in
  # CONDA_INSTALLATION_COMMANDS as a command-not-found. Repro'd on
  # a bare apt image (--image-id docker:ubuntu:18.04).
  #
  # Reintroducing the dpkg check is not an option: it is apt-only
  # (the point of this patch is RHEL/UBI/Alpine/SUSE), and it would
  # now DEADLOCK -- the install decision in STEP 1 uses binary
  # presence, so an image shipping curl outside dpkg is never
  # queued for install and a dpkg-state wait would spin forever.
  #
  # So gate on STEP 1's own marker instead. That is the package
  # manager reporting it returned, which is the "fully configured"
  # guarantee itself rather than a proxy for it -- portable across
  # apt/dnf/microdnf/yum/apk/zypper, and it needs no timeout or
  # per-distro CA paths. Also break out if STEP 1 failed, so this
  # can never outlive the step it waits on.
  until [ -f "$CORE_PKGS_READY" ] || [ -f "/tmp/${STEPS[0]}.failed" ]; do
    sleep 0.1
  done
  
  UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv -V >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | UV_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" sh;[ -d ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime ] || UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv venv --seed ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime --python 3.10;echo "$(echo ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime)/bin/python" > ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path;
  UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv -V >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | UV_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" sh;mkdir -p ~/sky_workdir && mkdir -p ~/.sky/sky_app && mkdir -p ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky;echo PATH=$PATH; VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv pip install "setuptools<70"; VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv pip install "click<8.3.0"; VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv pip list | grep "ray " | grep 2.9.3 2>&1 > /dev/null || RAY_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:6380 env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME $([ -s ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path ] && cat ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path 2> /dev/null || command -v python3) $([ -s ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/ray_path ] && cat ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/ray_path 2> /dev/null || command -v ray) status || VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv pip install -U "ray[default]==2.9.3" "pydantic-core==2.41.1" "click<8.3.0"; export PATH=$PATH:${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.local/bin; [ -s ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/ray_path ] || { VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv run --no-project --no-config sh -c "command -v ray" > ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/ray_path || exit 1; }; 

  # set UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON to false in case the user provided docker image set it to true.
  # unset PYTHONPATH and set CWD to $HOME to avoid user image interfering with SkyPilot runtime.
  VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME ~/.local/bin/uv pip install skypilot[kubernetes,remote]
  # Wait (bounded) for the best-effort `patch` install to land
  # before applying the Ray patches. An image may ship no `patch`
  # and have no usable repo, so proceed after 60s rather than hang
  # this step forever; the apply below is best-effort (see there).
  _patch_wait=0
  until command -v patch >/dev/null 2>&1; do
    sleep 0.1
    _patch_wait=$((_patch_wait + 1))
    if [ "$_patch_wait" -ge 600 ]; then
      echo "WARNING: patch not installed after 60s; proceeding."
      break
    fi
    # Throttle the notice to ~once every 5s (loop runs at 10Hz) so a
    # slow install doesn't flood the pod log 10x/second.
    if [ $((_patch_wait % 50)) -eq 1 ]; then
      echo "Waiting for patch package to be installed..."
    fi
  done
  # Apply Ray patches (quality-of-life fixes: progress bar, log
  # streaming). The patch payload is carried in this pod spec, not
  # read out of the installed `sky`: this runs before the SkyPilot
  # wheel is uploaded, so the only `sky` on the node is whatever
  # `pip install skypilot` resolved to -- an unrelated release,
  # whose patches target an unrelated Ray version. Reading them
  # from there corrupts Ray whenever the two disagree.
  # ray_patches_cmd self-guards on the Ray version it was
  # generated for, and says so when it skips.
  # Best-effort: apply_patches falls back to the Python `patch`
  # library when the system `patch` binary is absent, but on a
  # fully offline/minimal image that too can be unavailable. Warn
  # and continue rather than abort the launch -- the cluster comes
  # up and runs without these patches.
  if VIRTUAL_ENV=${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/skypilot-runtime UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=false env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME "$HOME/.local/bin"/uv pip list | grep "ray " | grep 2.9.3 > /dev/null 2>&1; then mkdir -p /tmp/sky_ray_patches && echo '' | base64 -d | tar xzf - -C /tmp/sky_ray_patches && env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME $([ -s ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path ] && cat ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path 2> /dev/null || command -v python3) /tmp/sky_ray_patches/apply_patches.py --ray-version 2.9.3; else echo "Ray 2.9.3 not found in the SkyPilot runtime env; skipping SkyPilot's Ray patches."; fi || echo "WARNING: could not apply Ray patches; continuing without them.";
  touch /tmp/ray_skypilot_installation_complete
  echo "=== Ray and skypilot installation completed ==="

  # Disable set -e, as we have some commands that are ok to fail
  # after the ray start.
  # TODO(zhwu): this is a hack, we should fix the commands that are
  # ok to fail.
  if [ "$SKYPILOT_POD_NODE_TYPE" == "head" ]; then
    set +e
    if [ "${SKYPILOT_HOST_NETWORK:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -n "${SKYPILOT_RAY_PORTS_CONFIGMAP_NAME:-}" ]; then echo '' | base64 -d | gunzip > /tmp/sky_host_network_probe.py; env -u PYTHONPATH -C $HOME $([ -s ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path ] && cat ${SKY_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME}/.sky/python_path 2> /dev/null || command -v python3) /tmp/sky_host_network_probe.py --mode head --env-file /tmp/sky_host_network_ports.env --configmap-name "$SKYPILOT_RAY_PORTS_CONFIGMAP_NAME" --configmap-namespace "$SKYPILOT_RAY_PORTS_CONFIGMAP_NAMESPACE" || exit 1; function mylsof { p=$(for pid in /proc/{0..9}*; do i=$(basename "$pid"); for file in "$pid"/fd/*; do link=$(readlink -e "$file"); if [ "$link" = "$1" ]; then echo "$i"; fi; done; done); echo "$p"; };

# Tails file and checks every 5 sec for
# open file handlers with write access
# closes if none exist
monitor_file() {
  local file="$1"
  tail -f "$file" &
  TAIL_PID=$!
  while kill -0 $TAIL_PID 2> /dev/null; do
    # only two PIDs should be accessing the file
    # the log appender and log tailer
    if [ $(mylsof "$file" | wc -l) -lt 2 ]; then
      kill $TAIL_PID
      break
    fi
    # Sleep for 5 seconds before checking again. Do not make this
    # too short as it will consume CPU, and too long will cause
    # the file to be closed too late keeping the pod alive.
    sleep 5
  done
}

log_tail() {
  # Use a bash glob (not `ls $(eval echo ...)`) so we are
  # safe against ARG_MAX at very high file counts and against
  # spaces in $HOME or in any path component. nullglob makes
  # an empty match a no-op instead of yielding the literal
  # pattern. log_tail is launched via `log_tail &`, so this
  # runs in its own subshell and the shopt does not leak.
  shopt -s nullglob

  # O(1) membership set. Replaces an `echo $str | grep -q` check
  # that was O(n) per file (O(n^2) across the outer loop).
  local -A already_monitored

  # Pre-seed with every file that exists at startup so we do NOT
  # spawn monitor_file for them. On an HA controller pod restart
  # the PVC retains task logs from all prior (completed) jobs;
  # tailing them all spawns a tail+mylsof loop per file, and
  # mylsof's /proc/*/fd/* scan grows with the process count,
  # producing runaway fork growth.
  for f in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log; do
    already_monitored["$f"]=1
  done

  # Wait until at least one log file exists.
  while true; do
    for f in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log; do
      break 2
    done
    sleep 1
  done

  # Infinite loop to continuously check for new files
  while true; do
    for file in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log; do
      if [[ -n "${already_monitored[$file]:-}" ]]; then
        # File is already being monitored
        continue
      fi

      # Monitor the new file
      monitor_file "$file" &
      already_monitored["$file"]=1
    done
    sleep 0.1
  done
}

    local tries=3
    local delay=1
    local i
    for i in $(seq 1 $tries); do

      ubuntu) APT_OS="ubuntu" ;;

            *ubuntu*) APT_OS="ubuntu" ;;
            *debian*) APT_OS="debian" ;;
          esac
        fi
        ;;
    esac

  # deb.debian.org is a CDN endpoint, if one backend goes down,
  # the CDN automatically fails over to another mirror,

  # and results from apt-select

  # Wrap the candidate-mirror loop in a function so we can
  # short-circuit when nothing needs installing.

    restore_source

      echo "Trying APT mirror ($APT_OS): $candidate" >> /tmp/apt-update.log
      found_sources=false
      if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list ]; then
        update_apt_sources $candidate /etc/apt/sources.list
        found_sources=true
      fi
      if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources ]; then
        update_apt_sources $candidate /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources
        found_sources=true
      fi

        dump_apt_log
        break
      fi

        echo "Install failed with ${candidate:-default sources}: $INSTALL_FIRST" >> /tmp/apt-update.log

      # package index for MISSING_PACKAGES.

    break

  # Non-apt install path (dnf/microdnf/yum/apk/zypper): mirror the

  run_pkg_install_nonapt() {
    INSTALL_SUCCESS=false
    if [ ! -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
      echo "Installing core packages via $PKG_MGR: $INSTALL_FIRST" >> /tmp/apt-update.log

      # candidates). A single transient repo/CDN/proxy failure
      # should not kill the launch.
      _core_try=0

        # runs under the `set -e` from the top of the install
        # section (unlike the apt path, which drops to `set +e`
        # inside its own helper). As a standalone command,
        # a non-zero pkg_install would abort STEP 1 right here --
        # before the _core_missing check, the sleep, or any retry
        # -- so the pod would fail with .failed instead of
        # retrying, defeating the point of this loop. It also
        # matters for zypper, whose >=100 informational-success
        # codes are non-zero. The exit status is deliberately
        # ignored; pkg_present below is what decides success.

        # a partially unreachable repo set is normal behind an
        # egress proxy. Ask the same portable question the install
        # decision asked -- is the package actually there now?
        _core_missing=""

    fi

    INSTALL_SUCCESS=true

  elif [ -n "$PKG_MGR" ]; then

  else

  # leaves set +e behind, and the non-apt / already-installed paths
  # must not differ from each other -- but the state they converge
  # on has to be set -e, because upstream ran this block under
  # set -e and the commands in it are load-bearing: if the
  # sshd_config edit, ssh-keygen or authorized_keys write fails,
  # SkyPilot cannot reach the pod at all. Swallowing those turns a
  # clear "apt-ssh-setup failed" into an opaque SSH timeout much
  # later. The genuinely optional Debian-isms are tolerated
  # individually with `|| true` at their own call sites instead.
  set -e

    exit 1
  fi;

  

  

  $(prefix_cmd) mkdir -p /var/run/sshd;
  $(prefix_cmd) sed -i "s/PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/" /etc/ssh/sshd_config;

  # a minimal non-Debian image -- so tolerate it rather than
  # dropping set -e for the load-bearing commands below.

  $(prefix_cmd) chmod 700 ~/.ssh;

SKYPILOT_SSH_KEY_EOF

  # `sshd` on RHEL/UBI/SUSE, and minimal containers often have no
  # service manager at all — fall back to launching the daemon
  # directly. `|| true` so a benign restart failure never aborts.
  $(prefix_cmd) service ssh restart 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) service sshd restart 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) systemctl restart ssh 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) systemctl restart sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) kill -HUP $(cat /var/run/sshd.pid 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) /usr/sbin/sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || $(prefix_cmd) /sbin/sshd 2>/dev/null \
    || true;

  # ~/.bash_profile) -- tolerate a missing file.
  $(prefix_cmd) sed -i "s/mesg n/tty -s \&\& mesg n/" ~/.profile || true;

  

  touch /tmp/apt_ssh_setup_complete
  echo "=== SSH setup completed ==="
  ) > /tmp/${STEPS[0]}.log 2>&1
  if [ "$?" -ne "0" ]; then
    {
    echo "Error: ${STEPS[0]} failed. Continuing anyway..." > /tmp/${STEPS[0]}.failed 2>&1
    cat /tmp/${STEPS[0]}.log
    exit 1
    }
  fi
) &

    # What actually broke on non-Debian images was not the `nc`
    # dialect -- Ncat does support `-z` (verified: nmap-ncat 7.92

    # Ncat, and keeps the probe to a connect test rather than
    # opening a data channel to a port that never closes.

  fi
  ) > /tmp/${STEPS[1]}.log 2>&1

    exit 1
    }

function mylsof { p=$(for pid in /proc/{0..9}*; do i=$(basename "$pid"); for file in "$pid"/fd/*; do link=$(readlink -e "$file"); if [ "$link" = "$1" ]; then echo "$i"; fi; done; done); echo "$p"; };

# Tails file and checks every 5 sec for
# open file handlers with write access
# closes if none exist
monitor_file() {
  local file="$1"
  tail -f "$file" &
  TAIL_PID=$!
  while kill -0 $TAIL_PID 2> /dev/null; do
    # only two PIDs should be accessing the file
    # the log appender and log tailer
    if [ $(mylsof "$file" | wc -l) -lt 2 ]; then
      kill $TAIL_PID
      break
    fi
    # Sleep for 5 seconds before checking again. Do not make this
    # too short as it will consume CPU, and too long will cause
    # the file to be closed too late keeping the pod alive.
    sleep 5
  done
}

log_tail() {
  # Use a bash glob (not `ls $(eval echo ...)`) so we are
  # safe against ARG_MAX at very high file counts and against
  # spaces in $HOME or in any path component. nullglob makes
  # an empty match a no-op instead of yielding the literal
  # pattern. log_tail is launched via `log_tail &`, so this
  # runs in its own subshell and the shopt does not leak.
  shopt -s nullglob

  # O(1) membership set. Replaces an `echo $str | grep -q` check
  # that was O(n) per file (O(n^2) across the outer loop).
  local -A already_monitored

  # Pre-seed with every file that exists at startup so we do NOT
  # spawn monitor_file for them. On an HA controller pod restart
  # the PVC retains task logs from all prior (completed) jobs;
  # tailing them all spawns a tail+mylsof loop per file, and
  # mylsof's /proc/*/fd/* scan grows with the process count,
  # producing runaway fork growth.
  for f in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log; do
    already_monitored["$f"]=1
  done

  # Wait until at least one log file exists.
  while true; do
    for f in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log; do
      break 2
    done
    sleep 1
  done

  # Infinite loop to continuously check for new files
  while true; do
    for file in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log; do
      if [[ -n "${already_monitored[$file]:-}" ]]; then
        # File is already being monitored
        continue
      fi

      # Monitor the new file
      monitor_file "$file" &
      already_monitored["$file"]=1
    done
    sleep 0.1
  done
}

# Wait for all three background setup steps to complete by
# polling their completion/failure markers. If any step fails,
# exit the container so the pod enters a failed state instead
# of hanging indefinitely.
STEP_COMPLETE_FILES=(/tmp/apt_ssh_setup_complete /tmp/ray_skypilot_installation_complete /tmp/env_setup_complete)
for i in "${!STEPS[@]}"; do
  until [ -f "${STEP_COMPLETE_FILES[$i]}" ] || [ -f "/tmp/${STEPS[$i]}.failed" ]; do
    sleep 1
  done
  if [ -f "/tmp/${STEPS[$i]}.failed" ]; then
    echo "Error: setup step '${STEPS[$i]}' failed. Pod will exit."
    exit 1
  fi
done


# Set +x to stop printing the commands and their arguments as they are executed.
set +x

# SIGTERM keep-alive: trap ignores TERM/INT so wait is not interrupted;
# log_tail streams task logs; sleep loop keeps the pod alive until killed.
trap : TERM INT
log_tail &
while true; do sleep infinity & wait $!; done
containers.name: ray-node

args:
# Set -x to print the commands and their arguments as they are executed.
# Useful for debugging.
set -x

# Execute user-provided post-provision runcmd
# before any of the SkyPilot setup commands.

# Helper function to conditionally use sudo
# TODO(zhwu): consolidate the two prefix_cmd and sudo replacements
prefix_cmd() { if [ $(id -u) -ne 0 ]; then echo "sudo"; else echo ""; fi; }
[ $(id -u) -eq 0 ] && function sudo() { "$@"; } || true;



STEPS=("apt-ssh-setup" "runtime-setup" "env-setup")

# Raise the open files limit before the STEPS below fork, so
# that ray (started by the "runtime-setup" STEP) inherits it;
# otherwise the raylet can run out of file descriptors while
# starting its workers. SSH sessions do not inherit from this
# shell -- sshd resets its own soft limit; they get theirs from
# the limits.conf entry written in setup_commands, applied by
# pam_limits at login.
ulimit -Sn 1048576 2>/dev/null || ulimit -Sn "$(ulimit -Hn)" || true

# Marker STEP 1 publishes once the CORE prereqs (curl/rsync/wget)
# are installed AND CONFIGURED -- i.e. the package manager has
# returned, not merely unpacked a binary. STEP 2 gates its HTTPS
# conda download on this; see the wait there for why binary
# presence alone is not enough. Declared out here so both step
# subshells see it. Published BEFORE the best-effort
# MISSING_PACKAGES install, so STEP 2 still overlaps with that and
# the INSTALL_FIRST/MISSING split keeps its purpose.
CORE_PKGS_READY=/tmp/sky_core_pkgs_ready

# STEP 1: Run apt update, install missing packages, and set up ssh.
(
  (
  # Timeout (seconds) for each individual apt-get invocation.
  # The default Acquire::http::Timeout is 120s which is too slow
  # when mirrors are degraded but not fully down.
  APT_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT=30
  APT_CMD_TIMEOUT=60
  APT_INSTALL_CMD_TIMEOUT=90
  APT_OPTS="-o Acquire::http::Timeout=${APT_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT} -o Acquire::https::Timeout=${APT_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT} -o Acquire::Retries=0"

  # Helper: run apt-get update with retries
  apt_update_with_retries() {
    # do not fail the whole shell; we handle return codes
    set +e
    local log=/tmp/apt-update.log
    local tries=3
    local delay=1
    local i
    for i in $(seq 1 $tries); do
      # apt-get update returns 0 even when sources fail to fetch,
      # so we also check output for failure indicators.
      local output
      output=$(timeout $APT_CMD_TIMEOUT $(prefix_cmd) env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update $APT_OPTS 2>&1)
      local rc=$?
      echo "$output" >> "$log"
      if [ $rc -eq 124 ]; then
        echo "apt-get update timed out after ${APT_CMD_TIMEOUT}s (attempt $i/$tries)" >> "$log"
      elif [ $rc -eq 0 ] && ! echo "$output" | grep -iq "Failed to fetch"; then
        set -e; return 0
      else
        echo "apt-get update attempt $i/$tries failed (rc=$rc)" >> "$log"
      fi
      [ $i -lt $tries ] && { echo "retrying in ${delay}s" >> "$log"; sleep $delay; delay=$((delay * 2)); }
    done
    set -e
    return 1
  }
  apt_install_with_retries() {
    local packages="$@"
    [ -z "$packages" ] && return 0
    set +e
    local log=/tmp/apt-update.log
    local tries=3
    local delay=1
    local i
    for i in $(seq 1 $tries); do
      timeout $APT_INSTALL_CMD_TIMEOUT \
        $(prefix_cmd) env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
        apt-get install $APT_OPTS -y \
        -o Dpkg::Options::="--force-confdef" \
        -o Dpkg::Options::="--force-confold" $packages
      local rc=$?
      if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then
        set -e; return 0
      elif [ $rc -eq 124 ]; then
        echo "apt-get install timed out after ${APT_INSTALL_CMD_TIMEOUT}s for: $packages (attempt $i/$tries)" >> "$log"
      else
        echo "apt-get install failed for: $packages (attempt $i/$tries, rc=$rc). Running -f install and retrying..." >> "$log"
      fi
      DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive $(prefix_cmd) apt-get -f install -y >> "$log" 2>&1 || true
      DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive $(prefix_cmd) apt-get clean >> "$log" 2>&1 || true
      [ $i -lt $tries ] && { echo "retrying in ${delay}s" >> "$log"; sleep $delay; delay=$((delay * 2)); }
    done
    set -e
    return 1
  }
  apt_update_install_with_retries() {
    apt_update_with_retries
    apt_install_with_retries "$@"
  }
  backup_dir=/etc/apt/sources.list.backup_skypilot
  backup_source() {
    $(prefix_cmd) mkdir -p "$backup_dir"
    if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list ] && [ ! -f "$backup_dir/sources.list" ]; then
      $(prefix_cmd) cp -a /etc/apt/sources.list "$backup_dir/sources.list" || true
    fi
    if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources ] && [ ! -f "$backup_dir/ubuntu.sources" ]; then
      $(prefix_cmd) cp -a /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources "$backup_dir/ubuntu.sources" || true
    fi
  }
  restore_source() {
    if [ -f "$backup_dir/sources.list" ]; then
      $(prefix_cmd) cp -a "$backup_dir/sources.list" /etc/apt/sources.list || true
    fi
    if [ -f "$backup_dir/ubuntu.sources" ]; then
      $(prefix_cmd) cp -a "$backup_dir/ubuntu.sources" /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources || true
    fi
  }
  update_apt_sources() {
    local host=$1
    local apt_file=$2

    # immutable bit, full tmpfs) shouldn't kill the whole step;
    # restore_source will undo any partial edits on the next
    # iteration of the candidate-mirror loop.
    $(prefix_cmd) sed -i -E "s|https?://[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\.ubuntu\.com/ubuntu|http://$host/ubuntu|g" "$apt_file" || true

  # Surface /tmp/apt-update.log to the pod's stderr on failure.
  # Without this, users only see the terse summary line — the
  # actual apt error stays inside the (often torn-down) pod.
  dump_apt_log() {
    local log=/tmp/apt-update.log
    if [ -f "$log" ]; then
      echo "=== /tmp/apt-update.log (last 200 lines) ===" >&2
      tail -n 200 "$log" >&2 || true
      echo "=== end /tmp/apt-update.log ===" >&2

      echo "/tmp/apt-update.log not found" >&2
    fi
  }
  # FUSE compatibility: we want libfuse2 (FUSE 2 ABI for legacy
  # clients like older s3fs/sshfs) AND fuse3 (binary + libfuse3-3
  # for hf-mount, rclone, blobfuse2, etc.). On Ubuntu 22.04+

  # two packages cannot coexist. FUSE is handled out-of-band below.
  PACKAGES="rsync curl wget netcat gcc patch pciutils openssh-server";

  # --- Portable package-manager support (CC-328 / TICKET-039) ---
  # This bootstrap historically assumed apt/dpkg (Debian/Ubuntu).
  # Detect the image's package manager, gate installs on BINARY
  # presence (`command -v`) rather than `dpkg -l`, and dispatch the
  # install through the right tool. Effect: a non-Debian image
  # (RHEL/UBI/Alpine/SUSE) that already ships the prereqs needs no
  # install at all; one that's missing them installs via dnf/apk/etc.
  # The apt path is UNCHANGED — INSTALL_FIRST/MISSING carry generic
  # names and map_pkg_names() translates them back to the exact apt
  # names (e.g. netcat -> netcat-openbsd) the old code used, so
  # Debian/Ubuntu behavior is byte-for-byte identical.
  PKG_MGR=""
  if   command -v apt-get  >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=apt
  elif command -v dnf      >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=dnf
  elif command -v microdnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=microdnf
  elif command -v yum      >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=yum
  elif command -v apk      >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=apk
  elif command -v zypper   >/dev/null 2>&1; then PKG_MGR=zypper
  fi

  # Is a generic package present? Prove via its BINARY (portable
  # across distros; `dpkg -l` doesn't exist on RHEL/Alpine/SUSE).
  pkg_present() {
    case "$1" in
      netcat)         command -v nc          >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;

      # already-present tool isn't needlessly (re)installed.
      openssh-server) command -v sshd  >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x /usr/sbin/sshd ]  || [ -x /sbin/sshd ]  ;;

      fuse3)          command -v fusermount3 >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;

    esac

  # Translate generic package names to per-manager names. apt names

  map_pkg_names() {
    local out="" g
    for g in "$@"; do

        netcat)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            dnf|yum|microdnf) out="$out nmap-ncat" ;;
            *)                out="$out netcat-openbsd" ;;
          esac ;;
        fuse)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            dnf|yum|microdnf) out="$out fuse fuse-libs" ;;
            *)                out="$out fuse" ;;
          esac ;;
        fuse3)
          case "$PKG_MGR" in
            dnf|yum|microdnf) out="$out fuse3 fuse3-libs" ;;
            *)                out="$out fuse3" ;;
          esac ;;

  # so that curl, rsync, ssh and wget are available sooner to unblock the following
  # conda installation and rsync.

  MISSING_PACKAGES="";

    # uses bash /dev/tcp (not `nc`), so netcat is not a launch blocker,

    case "$pkg" in

  # whatever trust store its curl uses), so STEP 2 has nothing to

  # paths, because several of those can bail out without being
  # fatal and would otherwise leave STEP 2 waiting forever:
  #   - apt with INSTALL_FIRST empty but MISSING_PACKAGES set: the
  #     index refresh can fail on every mirror and `continue` out
  #     of the loop, yet the core-install guard below only exits
  #     when INSTALL_FIRST is non-empty, so STEP 1 still ends 0.

  # Both cases are ones the old `command -v curl` gate passed
  # immediately, so not publishing here would be a regression.
  # Deliberately before the FUSE block below: `fuse` can be
  # appended to INSTALL_FIRST, but it has nothing to do with the
  # HTTPS conda download STEP 2 is gating on.
  if [ -z "$INSTALL_FIRST" ]; then
    touch "$CORE_PKGS_READY"
  fi

  #   (0, 0): install fuse first then fuse3. apt's Breaks
  #           resolution removes the `fuse` package while leaving
  #           libfuse2 → final state: libfuse2 (FUSE 2 ABI) +
  #           fuse3 (binary + libfuse3-3 for FUSE 3 ABI).
  #   (1, 0): only fuse3 missing. Queue it in MISSING_PACKAGES;
  #           apt removes `fuse` package but libfuse2 survives.
  #   (0, 1): already the desired state (SkyPilot default images).
  #           User-supplied images may lack libfuse2, need to handle
  #           this.
  #   (1, 1): impossible on Ubuntu 22.04+ (Breaks declaration);
  #           treated as no-op for forward-compat.
  

  # Detect distro for mirror fallback

  if [ -f /etc/os-release ]; then
    . /etc/os-release
    case "$ID" in
      debian) APT_OS="debian" ;;
      ubuntu) APT_OS="ubuntu" ;;
      *)
        if [ -n "$ID_LIKE" ]; then
          case " $ID $ID_LIKE " in
            *ubuntu*) APT_OS="ubuntu" ;;
            *debian*) APT_OS="debian" ;;
          esac
        fi

    esac

  # deb.debian.org is a CDN endpoint, if one backend goes down,
  # the CDN automatically fails over to another mirror,
  # so we only add mirror candidates for ubuntu here.
  # Selected from https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+archivemirrors
  # and results from apt-select
  
  MIRROR_CANDIDATES=""
  if [ "$APT_OS" = "ubuntu" ]; then
    MIRROR_CANDIDATES="mirrors.wikimedia.org mirror.umd.edu"
  fi
  

  # Wrap the candidate-mirror loop in a function so we can
  # short-circuit when nothing needs installing.

    restore_source

      echo "Trying APT mirror ($APT_OS): $candidate" >> /tmp/apt-update.log

      if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list ]; then
        update_apt_sources $candidate /etc/apt/sources.list
        found_sources=true

        update_apt_sources $candidate /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources
        found_sources=true
      fi

      echo "Installing core packages: $(map_pkg_names $INSTALL_FIRST)" >> /tmp/apt-update.log;
      apt_update_install_with_retries $(map_pkg_names $INSTALL_FIRST) >> /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1 || {
